title: 2 Timothy Chapter 1 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on 2 Timothy chapter 1 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: 2 Timothy Chapter 1 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of 2 Timothy Chapter 1.

questions.question: In 2 Timothy 1, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: Paul, an apostle of Jesus Christ
questions.correctAnswer: Paul, an apostle of Jesus Christ
questions.explanation: This is stated in the very first verse of the chapter, 2 Timothy 1:1.

questions.question: To whom is the letter of 2 Timothy addressed?
questions.explanation: The letter is addressed to Timothy as stated in 2 Timothy 1:2.

questions.question: What does Paul express in his prayers for Timothy?
questions.explanation: Paul mentions his remembrance of Timothy in his prayers night and day in 2 Timothy 1:3.

questions.question: What does Paul desire to see in Timothy?
questions.explanation: Paul states he is mindful of Timothy's tears, which he greatly desires to see in 2 Timothy 1:4.

questions.question: Who first had faith that dwelt in Timothy?
questions.explanation: Paul mentions that the unfeigned faith first dwelt in Timothy's grandmother Lois in 2 Timothy 1:5.

questions.question: What does Paul urge Timothy to stir up?
questions.explanation: Paul instructs Timothy to stir up the gift of God in 2 Timothy 1:6.

questions.question: What does Paul thank God for?
questions.explanation: Paul thanks God whom he serves from his forefathers with a pure conscience in 2 Timothy 1:3.

questions.question: From whom does grace, mercy, and peace come?
options: God the Father and Christ Jesus
questions.correctAnswer: God the Father and Christ Jesus
questions.explanation: Paul mentions that grace, mercy, and peace come from God the Father and Christ Jesus in 2 Timothy 1:2.

questions.question: What does Paul serve with?
questions.explanation: Paul serves God from his forefathers with a pure conscience as stated in 2 Timothy 1:3.

questions.question: What is the relationship between Paul and Timothy?
questions.explanation: Paul refers to Timothy as his dearly beloved son in 2 Timothy 1:2.

questions.question: What did Timothy's faith do in Paul?
questions.explanation: Paul hopes to be filled with joy when he sees Timothy, as he is mindful of Timothy's tears in 2 Timothy 1:4.

questions.question: When does Paul pray for Timothy?
questions.explanation: Paul states that he has remembrance of Timothy in his prayers night and day in 2 Timothy 1:3.

questions.question: Did Paul mention Timothy's mother in this chapter?
questions.explanation: Paul mentions Timothy's mother Eunice in 2 Timothy 1:5.

questions.question: Paul was an apostle of Peter.
questions.explanation: The text states that Paul is an apostle of Jesus Christ, not Peter, in 2 Timothy 1:1.

questions.question: Timothy was filled with joy when he prayed.
questions.explanation: The text mentions that Paul hopes to be filled with joy when he sees Timothy, not that Timothy was filled with joy while praying, in 2 Timothy 1:4.

medium.title: 2 Timothy Chapter 1 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from 2 Timothy Chapter 1 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What spirit has God given us according to 2 Timothy 1:7?
options: The spirit of power, love, and a sound mind
questions.correctAnswer: The spirit of power, love, and a sound mind
questions.explanation: This answer is correct because 2 Timothy 1:7 states that God has not given us the spirit of fear, but rather the spirit of power, love, and a sound mind.

questions.question: What does 2 Timothy 1:8 promise will happen if someone is not ashamed of the testimony of our Lord?
options: They will suffer afflictions of the gospel
questions.correctAnswer: They will suffer afflictions of the gospel
questions.explanation: This answer is correct because 2 Timothy 1:8 encourages not to be ashamed, indicating that partaking in the afflictions of the gospel will follow.

questions.question: Who has saved us and called us with a holy calling according to 2 Timothy 1:9?
questions.explanation: This answer is correct because 2 Timothy 1:9 explicitly states that God has saved us and called us with a holy calling.

questions.question: What does 2 Timothy 1:10 reveal about Jesus Christ?
questions.explanation: This answer is correct because 2 Timothy 1:10 states that Jesus Christ has abolished death and brought life and immortality to light through the gospel.

questions.question: What roles is Paul appointed to in 2 Timothy 1:11?
options: A preacher, an apostle, and a teacher of the Gentiles
questions.correctAnswer: A preacher, an apostle, and a teacher of the Gentiles
questions.explanation: This answer is correct as 2 Timothy 1:11 states that Paul is appointed as a preacher, apostle, and teacher of the Gentiles.

questions.question: What does Paul say in 2 Timothy 1:12 about his belief?
options: He knows whom he has believed
questions.correctAnswer: He knows whom he has believed
questions.explanation: This answer is correct because 2 Timothy 1:12 highlights Paul's firm belief in God and his assurance in what he has committed to Him.

questions.question: What does 2 Timothy 1:5 encourage Timothy to remember about his faith?
options: It is inherited from his father
questions.explanation: This answer is correct as 2 Timothy 1:5 mentions Timothy's unfeigned faith that first dwelt in his grandmother Lois and his mother Eunice.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the gift that Paul encourages Timothy to stir up in 2 Timothy 1:6?
questions.explanation: This answer is correct because 2 Timothy 1:6 encourages stirring up the gift of God for the purpose of fulfilling God's calling.

questions.question: What does 2 Timothy 1:3 express about Paul's feelings towards Timothy?
options: He is thankful and remembers him in prayer
questions.correctAnswer: He is thankful and remembers him in prayer
questions.explanation: This answer is correct because 2 Timothy 1:3 indicates Paul's constant remembrance of Timothy in prayer, reflecting his deep care and gratitude.

questions.question: What does Paul desire in 2 Timothy 1:4 regarding his relationship with Timothy?
options: To see him filled with joy
questions.correctAnswer: To see him filled with joy
questions.explanation: This answer is correct as 2 Timothy 1:4 shows Paul's desire to see Timothy, which would fill him with joy.

questions.question: What does 2 Timothy 1:2 express as a greeting to Timothy?
questions.explanation: This answer is correct as 2 Timothy 1:2 conveys Paul's greeting of grace, mercy, and peace from God the Father and Christ Jesus our Lord.

questions.question: Afflictions of the gospel are to be shared according to 2 Timothy 1:8. What does this imply about Christian suffering?
options: It is a burden to avoid
It is to be embraced as part of faith
It is a sign of weakness
questions.correctAnswer: It is to be embraced as part of faith
questions.explanation: This answer is correct because 2 Timothy 1:8 encourages participation in afflictions for the gospel, suggesting that suffering can be a part of faith.

questions.question: True or False: Paul expresses shame about his suffering for the gospel in 2 Timothy 1:12.
questions.explanation: This answer is correct because 2 Timothy 1:12 states that Paul is not ashamed of his suffering.

questions.question: True or False: According to 2 Timothy 1:9, our calling is based on our works.
questions.explanation: This answer is correct because 2 Timothy 1:9 states that our calling is not according to our works but according to God's purpose and grace.

questions.question: True or False: 2 Timothy 1:10 teaches that Jesus brought life and immortality to light through the gospel.
questions.explanation: This answer is correct because 2 Timothy 1:10 clearly states that Jesus brought life and immortality to light through the gospel.

hard.title: 2 Timothy Chapter 1 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from 2 Timothy Chapter 1.

questions.question: According to 2 Timothy 1:13, what is Timothy instructed to 'hold fast'?
questions.explanation: 2 Timothy 1:13 instructs Timothy to 'Hold fast the form of sound words, which thou hast heard of me, in faith and love which is in Christ Jesus.'

questions.question: In 2 Timothy 1:14, by what or whom is Timothy told to keep the 'good thing' committed to him?
options: The Holy Ghost which dwelleth in us
questions.correctAnswer: The Holy Ghost which dwelleth in us
questions.explanation: 2 Timothy 1:14 states, 'That good thing which was committed unto thee keep by the Holy Ghost which dwelleth in us.'

questions.question: Who are the two individuals mentioned in 2 Timothy 1:15 as having turned away from Paul?
questions.explanation: 2 Timothy 1:15 states, 'all they which are in Asia be turned away from me; of whom are Phygellus and Hermogenes.'

questions.question: What specific act of kindness is Onesiphorus commended for in 2 Timothy 1:16?
options: Refreshing Paul and not being ashamed of his chains
questions.correctAnswer: Refreshing Paul and not being ashamed of his chains
questions.explanation: 2 Timothy 1:16 says, 'The Lord give mercy unto the house of Onesiphorus; for he oft refreshed me, and was not ashamed of my chain:'

questions.question: Where was Paul when Onesiphorus diligently sought him out, according to 2 Timothy 1:17?
questions.explanation: 2 Timothy 1:17 states, 'But, when he was in Rome, he sought me out very diligently, and found me.'

questions.question: What is the prayer concerning Onesiphorus in 2 Timothy 1:18?
options: That he may find mercy of the Lord in that day
That he may be healed from sickness
That he may become a great apostle
That he may receive great wealth
questions.correctAnswer: That he may find mercy of the Lord in that day
questions.explanation: 2 Timothy 1:18 prays, 'The Lord grant unto him that he may find mercy of the Lord in that day.'

questions.question: What does the Greek word 'parakaleo' used in 2 Timothy 1:6 mean?
questions.explanation: The Greek verb 'parakaleo' (παρακαλέω) commonly means 'to urge,' 'to encourage,' or 'to stir up,' which fits 2 Timothy 1:6 where Paul tells Timothy to 'stir up the gift of God.'

questions.question: Which literary device is prominently used in 2 Timothy 1:3-4 where Paul recalls Timothy's tears and expresses desire to see him?
questions.explanation: 2 Timothy 1:3-4 employs pathos by evoking deep emotional connection through Paul's remembrance of Timothy's tears and his desire to see him, appealing to feelings of affection and sorrow.

questions.question: Which Old Testament passage echoes the theme of faith being passed through generations as seen in 2 Timothy 1:5?
questions.explanation: Psalm 78:4 emphasizes telling the next generation the praiseworthy deeds of the Lord, echoing 2 Timothy 1:5 where unfeigned faith is remembered through Lois and Eunice to Timothy.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage connects with 2 Timothy 1:7's theme of God giving a spirit not of fear but of power, love, and a sound mind?
questions.explanation: Romans 8:15 speaks of receiving the Spirit of adoption, not of bondage to fear, aligning with 2 Timothy 1:7's teaching that God gives a spirit of power, love, and a sound mind.

questions.question: What comes immediately before Paul telling Timothy to 'Hold fast the form of sound words' in 2 Timothy 1:13?
options: Paul's confidence in God who keeps what he has committed
Paul's greeting of grace, mercy, and peace
Paul's instructions to not be ashamed of the gospel
Paul's mention of Timothy's unfeigned faith
questions.correctAnswer: Paul's confidence in God who keeps what he has committed
questions.explanation: 2 Timothy 1:12 immediately precedes verse 13, where Paul expresses he is not ashamed because he knows whom he believed and is persuaded God can keep what he has committed.

questions.question: The exhortation in 2 Timothy 1:8 to not be ashamed reflects what cultural reality of the early Christian era?
options: Persecution and social stigma against Christians
Freedom of religion in the Roman Empire
questions.correctAnswer: Persecution and social stigma against Christians
questions.explanation: 2 Timothy 1:8 urges Timothy not to be ashamed of the testimony, reflecting the historical context of persecution and social stigma Christians faced in the Roman world.

questions.question: How does 2 Timothy 1:10 typologically foreshadow the Christian hope in resurrection?
options: By stating Jesus abolished death and brought life and immortality to light
questions.correctAnswer: By stating Jesus abolished death and brought life and immortality to light
questions.explanation: 2 Timothy 1:10 foreshadows resurrection hope typologically by declaring Jesus abolished death and revealed life and immortality, fulfilling messianic promises.

questions.question: True or False: According to 2 Timothy 1:7, God has given believers a spirit of fear.
questions.explanation: 2 Timothy 1:7 states clearly, 'For God hath not given us the spirit of fear; but of power, and of love, and of a sound mind.'

questions.question: True or False: Paul indicates in 2 Timothy 1:15 that all in Asia remained loyal to him.
questions.explanation: 2 Timothy 1:15 explicitly states that 'all they which are in Asia be turned away from me,' indicating disloyalty, including Phygellus and Hermogenes.

theological.title: 2 Timothy Chapter 1 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from 2 Timothy Chapter 1 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does 2 Timothy 1:9 teach about salvation?
options: Salvation is according to our works and human effort
Salvation is a holy calling given according to God's purpose and grace, not works
Salvation is a result of human faith alone without God's initiative
Salvation is conditional on fulfilling the law perfectly
questions.correctAnswer: Salvation is a holy calling given according to God's purpose and grace, not works
questions.explanation: 2 Timothy 1:9 states that God has saved us and called us with a holy calling, not according to our works, but according to His own purpose and grace.

questions.question: What doctrine about the Holy Spirit does 2 Timothy 1:14 teach?
options: The Holy Spirit indwells believers and preserves the gospel entrusted to them
The Holy Spirit is only a temporary helper who leaves after conversion
The Holy Spirit is unrelated to the preservation of sound doctrine
The Holy Spirit must be earned by works to remain in believers
questions.correctAnswer: The Holy Spirit indwells believers and preserves the gospel entrusted to them
questions.explanation: 2 Timothy 1:14 instructs Timothy to keep the good thing committed to him by the Holy Ghost which dwelleth in us, indicating the Spirit's role in indwelling and preserving the gospel.

questions.question: What doctrine does 2 Timothy 1:7 teach about the nature of the Spirit given to believers?
options: God gives a spirit of fear to keep believers humble
God gives a spirit of power, love, and a sound mind, not of fear
God gives a spirit of confusion and uncertainty
God gives a spirit that causes believers to be timid and weak
questions.correctAnswer: God gives a spirit of power, love, and a sound mind, not of fear
questions.explanation: 2 Timothy 1:7 clearly states that God hath not given us the spirit of fear; but of power, and of love, and of a sound mind.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does 2 Timothy 1:12 specifically demonstrate?
options: God's faithfulness to keep what is committed to Him
questions.correctAnswer: God's faithfulness to keep what is committed to Him
questions.explanation: 2 Timothy 1:12 emphasizes Paul's confidence that God is able to keep what he has committed unto Him until that day, demonstrating God's faithfulness.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does 2 Timothy 1:9 reveal about God in salvation?
questions.explanation: 2 Timothy 1:9 shows God calling us with a holy calling according to His own purpose and grace, indicating His covenant faithfulness in salvation.

questions.question: How does 2 Timothy 1:10 connect to the broader biblical theme of resurrection and eternal life?
options: It denies the resurrection and focuses solely on moral living
It affirms that Christ abolished death and brought life and immortality to light through the gospel
It teaches reincarnation instead of resurrection
It presents eternal life as attainable by works alone
questions.correctAnswer: It affirms that Christ abolished death and brought life and immortality to light through the gospel
questions.explanation: 2 Timothy 1:10 states that Christ abolished death and brought life and immortality to light through the gospel, connecting to the biblical theme of resurrection and eternal life.

questions.question: How does the mention of Onesiphorus in 2 Timothy 1:16-17 serve the narrative arc of faithful ministry in Scripture?
options: It shows the rejection of all companions by Paul
It exemplifies faithful support and courage in suffering for the gospel
It emphasizes the futility of Christian fellowship
It highlights the superiority of some apostles over others
questions.correctAnswer: It exemplifies faithful support and courage in suffering for the gospel
questions.explanation: Verses 16-17 commend Onesiphorus for diligently seeking Paul and not being ashamed of his chains, illustrating faithful support amid suffering, a recurring biblical theme.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do verses 6 and 7 teach about Christian empowerment?
options: The gift of God is stirred up by human strength alone and fear is a sign of faith
Believers must stir up the gift of God and God gives a spirit of power, love, and a sound mind, not fear
The gift of God is irrelevant and fear is necessary for obedience
The Spirit given is fearful and weak, requiring human effort to overcome
questions.correctAnswer: Believers must stir up the gift of God and God gives a spirit of power, love, and a sound mind, not fear
questions.explanation: 2 Timothy 1:6 exhorts stirring up the gift of God, and 1:7 clarifies God gives a spirit of power, love, and sound mind, teaching the doctrine of empowered sanctification.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do 2 Timothy 1:13 and 1:14 teach about the preservation of doctrine and faith?
options: Sound doctrine is to be held loosely and can be changed freely
Believers should hold fast to the form of sound words in faith and love, guarded by the Holy Spirit
Faith is independent of doctrine and the Holy Spirit is not involved in preservation
Love is unrelated to sound doctrine and the Spirit does not dwell in believers
questions.correctAnswer: Believers should hold fast to the form of sound words in faith and love, guarded by the Holy Spirit
questions.explanation: 2 Timothy 1:13 commands holding fast sound doctrine in faith and love, while 1:14 states the Holy Spirit guards this trust, teaching preservation of faith and doctrine by the Spirit.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do 2 Timothy 1:1 and 1:11 teach about Paul's apostolic authority and mission?
options: Paul's apostleship is self-appointed and unrelated to Christ's will
Paul is appointed by the will of God to preach and teach the Gentiles as apostle of Jesus Christ
Paul's mission excludes teaching and focuses only on miracles
Paul's authority is based on political power
questions.correctAnswer: Paul is appointed by the will of God to preach and teach the Gentiles as apostle of Jesus Christ
questions.explanation: 2 Timothy 1:1 states Paul is an apostle by the will of God, and 1:11 says he is appointed preacher, apostle, and teacher of the Gentiles, revealing his divinely authorized mission.

questions.question: Skeptics claim that 2 Timothy 1:8-9 teaches salvation is earned by suffering for the gospel. What does this passage actually teach?
options: Salvation is earned by enduring suffering for the gospel
Believers should not be ashamed of the gospel and share in its afflictions, but salvation is by God's purpose and grace
Suffering is irrelevant to the Christian life
Salvation depends on human works rather than God's calling
questions.correctAnswer: Believers should not be ashamed of the gospel and share in its afflictions, but salvation is by God's purpose and grace
questions.explanation: 2 Timothy 1:8 encourages sharing in gospel afflictions without shame, while 1:9 clarifies salvation is by God's purpose and grace, not works or suffering.

questions.question: What doctrine about intergenerational faith does 2 Timothy 1:5 teach?
options: Faith is only individual and unrelated to family heritage
Unfeigned faith can be passed down through generations, as seen in Timothy's grandmother and mother
Faith is inherited genetically and unchangeable
Faith is irrelevant and personal only
questions.correctAnswer: Unfeigned faith can be passed down through generations, as seen in Timothy's grandmother and mother
questions.explanation: 2 Timothy 1:5 recalls the genuine faith in Timothy that first dwelt in his grandmother Lois and mother Eunice, teaching the doctrine of faith passed through godly heritage.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is highlighted in 2 Timothy 1:10 regarding Christ's redemptive work?
options: God's power in abolishing death and revealing life and immortality
questions.correctAnswer: God's power in abolishing death and revealing life and immortality
questions.explanation: 2 Timothy 1:10 describes Christ abolishing death and bringing life and immortality to light through the gospel, demonstrating God's powerful redemption.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do 2 Timothy 1:3 and 1:4 teach about prayer and pastoral concern?
options: Prayer is unnecessary for pastoral ministry
Paul's continual prayer and longing for Timothy's presence reflects pastoral love and concern
Pastoral care is limited to teaching only
Prayer is only for public worship and not personal
questions.correctAnswer: Paul's continual prayer and longing for Timothy's presence reflects pastoral love and concern
questions.explanation: 2 Timothy 1:3-4 show Paul praying night and day for Timothy and desiring to see him to be filled with joy, teaching the doctrine of pastoral love expressed in prayer.

questions.question: What doctrine about apostolic suffering and confidence is taught in 2 Timothy 1:12?
options: Paul is ashamed of his sufferings and doubts his faith
Paul suffers without shame because he knows whom he has believed and trusts God to guard his deposit
Faith is uncertain and cannot sustain suffering
questions.correctAnswer: Paul suffers without shame because he knows whom he has believed and trusts God to guard his deposit
questions.explanation: 2 Timothy 1:12 states Paul is not ashamed of his sufferings because he is confident in God’s ability to keep what he entrusted to Him, teaching apostolic confidence amid suffering.
